stories.working_title: The bug that only appears when you delete the model
the_decision_it_is_about: Running the whole pipeline with the interpreter removed, as an ablation,
to see how much of the result the model is actually responsible for.
what_happened: The covered count went up when the model was removed: 31 became 32. A
check that fails open looks like a check that passes, and it looks most
like one exactly when the thing it depends on is missing.
Two fail-opens came out of it. Continuity was blocking only on CONFLICTING
rather than on any exception state, and a beat was being counted covered
without its coverage finding being VERIFIED. Both are one-line changes and
neither was visible in a passing test suite.
The general shape: absent evidence has to be a finding. An ablation is the
cheapest way to find the places where it silently became a pass.
aws_content: The ablation runs against the local adapters that implement the same ports
as the deployed Lambda, so it needs no account to reproduce.

stories.working_title: An approval should expire when the evidence moves
the_decision_it_is_about: Binding a human decision to the SHA-256 of the finding it was taken about,
rather than to the finding's id.
what_happened: Finding ids are deterministic, so `<run>:con:CR-01` is the same string
before and after a rerun. A supervisor could accept a continuity conflict
as intentional, a new take could change the evidence completely, the
finding would be recomputed, and the old acceptance would still close it.
Nobody would have looked at the new facts and nothing would have said so.
The fix is small: HumanDecision carries finding_sha256, and the gate skips
a decision whose bound digest no longer matches. The interface consequence
is larger. The page cannot simply drop the approval, because an approval
that vanishes is its own confusion, so it says which decision no longer
applies and why, and puts the control back.
Building this on Strands surfaced a related property worth stating: on
resume a tool body replays from its first line, so any external effect has
to sit after the interrupt behind an idempotency key or it fires twice.
aws_content: Every HTTP request is a separate Lambda invocation and the run is rebuilt
from S3 each time, so the pause between a checkpoint and an approval
genuinely crosses a process boundary rather than holding a stack frame.
Strands S3SessionManager persists the session; Aurora DSQL holds run state.

stories.working_title: Three defects a browser test found that a green suite did not
the_decision_it_is_about: Treating browser to API to persistent state to visible result as the unit
of done, and running it against the deployed URL rather than a local build.
what_happened: A beat click in the test landed on a take pill, because a scripted click
skips hit testing and a real cursor does not. That was a real overlap.
A page-level refusal never reached the form. The API returned the missing
field name; the browser layer treated every non-200 as a failure to answer
and put a one-line error in a banner at the top of the page instead. The
form's own output stayed empty and the field names were discarded by the
code that had asked for them.
A click during a background request vanished entirely. Accepting an
exception posts one request and chains a second, and a button pressed
during the second was swallowed with no message, because the guard
returned early and the button was static markup that no repaint had told.
None of the three was reachable from unit tests, and all three were on the
deployed build with a green suite behind them.
